newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Discovery, Premier in contact.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Discovery, Premier in contact.

text.p: Takeover target Discovery Petroleum NL told shareholders on Monday no formal talks were underway with suitor Premier Oil Australia Pty Ltd over a higher offer although officials of both companies later acknowledged the companies have had some contact.

Discovery directors have urged shareholders in the Australia-based energy company, which also holds assets in Indonesia, to reject Premier's offer of A$0.70 a share, claiming it undervalues the company.
Citing an independent study, Discovery values its shares between $A0.77 and A$0.95 a share.
Discovery's chairman, Peter Jones, told Discovery's annual shareholders meeting here that "no formal indication to the board" had been made of an increase in the offer by Premier.

However, though no new offer has been mentioned, Eric Streitberg, chief executive of Discovery, and Steve Lowden, general manager of the international division of Premier Oil Plc of the United Kingdom, which owns 100 percent of Premier Oil Australia, told Reuters separately there have been talks among the two parties.
Lowden attended the Discovery annual meeting.
Streitberg also said Discovery has held its own talks with Oil Search Ltd an Australia-listed company whose assets are located in Papua New Guinea.
Since the Premier offer, Oil Search has acquired a 10.1 percent stake in Discovery, paying A$0.75 a share, seven percent above the Premier offer.
Oil Search is Discovery's single largest shareholder.
Streitberg said Oil Search has not said whether it intends to launch a counter bid for Discovery.

Discovery's main producing assests are located in the Kakap region of Indonesia, where it holds an 18.75 percent interest in the West Natunal Basin. Premier holds its own Indonesian assets nearby Discovery's interests.
Discovery also holds stakes in oil and gas and condensate production in the Perth and Otway Basins and in the Timor Sea and in the Taranaki Basin in New Zealand.
Lowden rejected claims by some analysts that Premier solely favours Discovery's Indonesian assets and has little interest in potentially exploiting the company's Australian interests.
"We wouldn't be here if that was the case," Lowden told Reuters.
Streitberg said Discovery was close to negotiating an A$13 million farm-out exploration agreement with a company over its Perth Basin assets.
Premier's offer for Discovery is subject to a minimum 50.1 percent acceptance.
